html:
SMTO-PRX-0005 — Proxmox mutation outcome is unknown

GUID: b269c595-1e46-4e7e-b6e4-66eb434d7412
Slug: proxmox-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: PRX · Subsystem: prx

What happened

  • SMTO sent a change to Proxmox but never got a clear answer about whether it worked. The change may already have happened, so SMTO won't send it again by itself.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the Proxmox web interface and look at the machine's current state, for example whether it is running or stopped. The machine's state shows whether the change took effect.
  2. Check the Proxmox task log for a recent task on that machine and whether it finished. A finished task confirms Proxmox carried out the change.
  3. Tell SMTO what you found, and ask it to repeat the change only if it did not happen. Repeating it blindly could, for example, reboot a machine twice.
  4. If a shutdown is still in progress, let it finish rather than asking for a forced stop. A forced stop can lose unsaved work on the machine.

What success looks like

  • Proxmox shows the machine in the state you wanted, and SMTO continues without repeating the change.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again. If you can't tell, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages your Proxmox server. Don't ask SMTO to force-stop the machine because a shutdown seemed stuck.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Proxmox write returned effect_unknown or lost its response, or a power action lost its session before completion could be confirmed; the change was kept as uncertain and not replayed.

What this means

  • A write returns effect_unknown, or a power mutation loses trustworthy completion/session evidence and is preserved as uncertain even after a reconciliation read. Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.

Why this can happen

  • A write returns effect_unknown, or a power mutation loses trustworthy completion/session evidence and is preserved as uncertain even after a reconciliation read.

How to diagnose it

  • Correlate the original task/guest state; a matching running state alone cannot prove a reboot/reset occurred.

How to fix it

  • Read the live guest state and the Proxmox task log (matching the task's UPID if one was recorded) to determine whether the write took effect before any further change. Never replay the write blindly or escalate a graceful shutdown to a forced stop.
  • Inspect live guest and task state before repeating a mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Authoritative original task evidence establishes the outcome before any further mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Proxmox task and resource receipts own effect truth. A failed read, expired local wait or invalid response does not undo a mutation; diagnostics never replay writes or escalate graceful shutdown to forced stop.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
